name: Firefly Field
summary: A summer night reflex game: tap fireflies while they glow to fill a glass jar before the moon sets
about: A full-screen meadow at dusk with rolling hills, a cottage window, a fence, swaying long grass and a moon that crosses the sky as your timer. Fireflies blink for a moment and you catch each one while it glows; it streaks into a glass jar that brightens as it fills, and a full jar opens to let them all float into the sky. Later nights blink faster, send chains of fireflies that light up in a row and add moths you must not touch.
how: A demo night plays on load; press My turn, Play, any field key or tap the meadow to start.
Click or tap a firefly while it glows; with the keyboard, Q W E, A S D and Z X C (or the number pad) each catch the brightest glow in that ninth of the field.
Quick catches add a bonus, every five in a row raises the multiplier, and catching a whole chain of four adds 500.
Touching a moth breaks your streak and costs one of three lives; the night ends when the moon sets.
Fill the jar to clear the night and move on to a faster one; P or Escape pauses and R restarts.
Your best score is saved on this device, crickets and chimes are made live in the browser and reduced motion calms the grass and shaking.
